predecessors.name: Rössen culture
predecessors.text: the Rössen country on which the Michelsberg appears: 'Preceded by: Rössen culture, Cerny culture'

successors.name: Wartberg Culture
successors.text: northern Hesse and western Thuringia, where the Wartberg culture 'appears to be a regional development derived from Michelsberg' (drawn as a 130 km disc at Kassel inside the Michelsberg shape)

ledger.x: 4400 BCE: the Michelsberg culture emerges in northeastern France.

4300 BCE: the Michelsberg spreads over the Rhine land of central Germany and eastern Belgium. the page says it spread through central Germany, northeastern France and eastern Belgium but gives no year, so the date is bridged from the end of the Rössen.

4300 BCE: the Michelsberg reaches the southwestern Netherlands and Belgian Luxembourg. the page says it reached the southwestern Netherlands; no year on the page (bridged to -4300), and the page is silent on who held the land, so it is recorded as nobody's.
3500 BCE: the Michelsberg ends over most of its country.

certainty.note: A prehistoric culture known from its enclosures; the page gives no frontier, and the extent is the researcher's reading of country and region names.
